item.aggregated_output:
# Policies

An AI agent that is asked to make a test pass will also lengthen a method, add a `Helper` class, open a new section in the README or lower the PHPStan level, if nothing stops it. Each of those changes looks reasonable alone. Guard declares what the project has decided about them in `guard.yaml`, reports every change that departs from it, and repairs the departures that have exactly one correct fix.

## Policies

| Section | What it checks | Rule IDs | Repaired by `fix` |
|---------|----------------|----------|---------------------|
| `metrics` | Lines and cyclomatic complexity of PHP files, classes, functions and methods. See [metrics](metrics.md). | `metrics.*` | no |
| `structure` | What each directory may contain, how entries are named, and how many there are. See [structure](structure.md). | `structure.*` | no |
| `documentation` | The headings, outline, badges or exact content of Markdown files, and Markdown files nobody declared. See [documents](documents.md). | `documentation.*` | no |
| `configuration` | Values in the configuration files of other tools, such as `phpstan.neon` or `phpunit.xml.dist`. See [configuration fields](fields.md). | the rule's `id` | yes, when the rule has a repair |
| `test_dependencies` | Composer development namespaces and Deptrac dependency boundaries for test directories. See [test dependencies](fields.md#test-dependencies). | `test-dependencies.*` | yes, including a missing Deptrac file |
| `benchmarks` | PHPBench directory contents, filenames, namespace references and Composer commands. See [benchmarks](benchmarks.md). | `phpbench.*` | Composer fields only |
| `extensions` | Whatever a project or a package adds. See [extensions](extensions.md). | chosen by the extension | when the extension proposes a change |

A section that `guard.yaml` neither writes nor [imports](configuration.md#imports) is not checked.

## Required and recommended

Every finding is either required or recommended. A required finding is reported as `error` and fails the command with exit code `1`. A recommendation is reported as `warning` and leaves the exit code at `0`. Configuration rules choose their level with `level`; metric, structure and document findings are always required.

## What is repaired

`guard fix` only writes configuration fields. A field has one value that satisfies its rule, or a declared fallback, so writing it is a deterministic edit. Splitting a method, renaming a class or rewriting a section is not, so those findings remain until someone edits the code or the document.

Each message names the offending file and symbol, what the policy expects, and how to comply. It also says that changing the declaration itself needs a human to update `guard.yaml`, so an agent fixes the project instead of the policy.

## Workflow

1. Run `guard init` to write a `guard.yaml` that imports the presets matching the project. See [init](cli.md#init).
2. Review the file, adjust thresholds and declarations in the [configuration](configuration.md), and commit it.
3. Run `guard fix --dry-run`, then `guard fix`, to bring the tool configuration in line.
4. Fix the remaining findings in code and documents until `guard check` passes.
5. Run `guard check` in CI. When a finding reflects a deliberate decision, a human changes `guard.yaml` in the same change.

## What it does not prove

Guard checks shape: sizes, names, headings and values. A short method can still be wrong, and a README with the declared sections can still be out of date. Passing `guard check` means the project has not drifted from what was decided, not that the decisions are good.
# Configuration

`guard.yaml` declares the policies of a project. Commands read `guard.yaml` in the working directory; pass `--config FILE` to use another. Every path in it is relative to the directory of the main `guard.yaml`, whatever the working directory and wherever an import lives.

## Example

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/metrics.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/structure.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/phpstan.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/readme-md.yaml
metrics:
  source: [src]
  profiles:
    standard:
      limits:
        file: {lines: 800}
documentation:
  scan: ['*.md']
configuration:
  - id: phpstan.level
    level: recommended
```

The imports supply the shipped rules; the rest of the file changes only what this project does differently. Here the file length limit is raised, every Markdown file in the root must be declared, and the PHPStan level becomes a recommendation instead of a requirement.

## Fields

| Key | Required | Description |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| `version` | yes | Always `1`. An imported file may omit it. |
| `imports` | no | Other policy files to load first. See [Imports](#imports). |
| `collect` | no | The files Guard may read at all. See [Collection scope](#collection-scope). |
| `metrics` | no | PHP size and complexity limits. See [metrics](metrics.md). |
| `structure` | no | Directory rules. See [structure](structure.md). |
| `documentation` | no | Markdown document declarations. See [documents](documents.md). |
| `configuration` | no | Rules for values in tool configuration files. See [configuration fields](fields.md). |
| `test_dependencies` | no | PSR-4 mappings and Deptrac boundaries for root test directories. See [test dependencies](fields.md#test-dependencies). |
| `benchmarks` | no | Set `true` to require the PHPBench layout and Composer commands for `bench/`. See [benchmarks](benchmarks.md). |
| `extensions` | no | Extension classes and their options, as `Class: {options}`. See [extensions](extensions.md). |

Unknown keys, invalid types, contradictory bounds and two `configuration` rules with the same `id` in one file are errors with exit code `2`. Error messages name a section by the file it came from historically, such as `tree.yaml` for `structure` or `doc-guard.yaml` for `documentation`.

## Imports

Each entry of `imports` is a path relative to the file that lists it, or an absolute path. An imported file may import more files. Guard loads the imports in order and then applies the file itself, so a later import overrides an earlier one and the project file overrides all of them. A circular import is an error.

An override keeps every imported value it does not mention:

| Key | Merged by |
|-----|-----------|
| `collect.include`, `collect.exclude` | Each list replaces the imported one when set. |
| `metrics.profiles` | Profile name. A profile replaces only the keys it sets, and inside `limits` only the metrics it sets. |
| `metrics.source`, `metrics.exclude`, `metrics.default`, `metrics.assignments` | Each replaces the imported value when set. |
| `structure.directories` | `path`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new path is added. |
| `structure.paths`, `structure.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |
| `documentation.files` | Document path. A declaration replaces only the keys it sets, so a project can add `headings` to a document whose `outlines` come from a preset. |
| `documentation.scan`, `documentation.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |
| `configuration` | `id`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new `id` is added. |
| `test_dependencies` | The whole settings mapping is replaced; omitted settings use their defaults. |
| `benchmarks` | The boolean is replaced. `false` disables an imported benchmark policy. |
| `extensions` | Class name. A later declaration replaces that class's whole option mapping and keeps its position. |

To drop an imported rule, remove the import and write the rules you want in the project file instead. A policy without `imports` is a complete custom policy.

## Presets

The package ships presets in `vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/`. Import only those you want; [`guard init`](cli.md#init) selects the ones that match the project.

| Preset | Checks |
|--------|--------|
| `metrics.yaml` | The standard [metric limits](metrics.md#limits) for `src`. |
| `structure.yaml` | The standard [directory rules](structure.md) for `src`, `tests/Unit` and `skills`, scanning from the project root. |
| `disable-doc.yaml` | No `docs/` directory in the project root, even an empty one. |
| `readme-md.yaml` | The outline and badges of `README.md`. See [documents](documents.md#shipped-declarations). |
| `agents-md.yaml` | The outline of `AGENTS.md`. |
| `claude-md.yaml` | `CLAUDE.md` contains exactly `@AGENTS.md`. |
| `phpstan.yaml`, `phpstan-guard-rules.yaml` | PHPStan level, includes and toolkit rules. |
| `phpunit9.yaml` … `phpunit13.yaml` | The PHPUnit configuration of each major. |
| `doctest9.yaml` … `doctest13.yaml` | The doctest suite in the PHPUnit configuration of each major. |
| `php-cs-fixer.yaml`, `phpcs.yaml`, `deptrac.yaml`, `infection.yaml`, `composer.yaml` | The configuration of each tool. |
| `github-actions.yaml`, `mutation.yaml` | The CI workflow and the scheduled mutation workflow. |
| `test-dependencies.yaml` | Independent `bench/`, `fuzz/`, `spec/`, and `tests/` namespaces and Deptrac layers, each allowed to depend only on production layers under `src/`. |
| `pbt.yaml` | Property tests under `tests/Property` with `*Properties.php` filenames and Composer scripts selecting the `unit` and `property` PHPUnit suites. `guard init` adds the property suite and suffix requirements to each selected PHPUnit configuration. |
| `phpbench.yaml` | The flat `bench/` directory, PHPBench namespace references, and repairable Composer mappings and commands. |
| `fuzz.yaml`, `docgen.yaml` | The configuration of each tool, for projects that use it. |

## Collection scope

`collect` limits which files Guard reads. Every policy, built-in or from an extension, sees only what lies inside it:

```text
files a policy sees = (collect.include − collect.exclude) ∩ files the policy asks for
```

```yaml
version: 1
collect:
  include: [src, docs, README.md, schemas/catalog.xsd]
  exclude: ['**/generated/**', 'docs/archive/**']
```

| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `include` | `['**']` | Paths and globs to read. A directory includes everything below it. `[]` selects nothing. |
| `exclude` | `[]` | Paths and globs removed from `include`. An excluded directory is skipped with everything below it. |

`*` matches within one path segment and `**` matches any number of segments. Absolute paths, `..` and backslashes are rejected. Symbolic links are not followed.

When `collect` is set, it replaces the per-section reading scopes `metrics.source` and `metrics.exclude`, `structure.paths` and `structure.exclude`, and `documentation.exclude`, including values from presets. Metrics then read every `.php` file in the scope. Assignments, directory rule paths, declared documents, scan patterns and configuration rule files still choose what each policy checks.

A file outside the scope is treated as if a policy had not asked for it: a declared document or configuration file outside the scope is skipped, not reported as missing. Without `collect`, each section keeps its own scope settings.

Guard walks the file system once for all policies, reads each file at most once and parses it at most once per format, however many policies ask for it.

## Enabling and Disabling Rules

Rules inherit `toolkit.allRules`, which defaults to `true`, except mutation
contracts, which are opt-in so an existing unannotated project does not change
semantics on upgrade. Override a specific rule through its `enabled` value:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        forbidEmptyCatch:
            enabled: false
```

Set `allRules: false` to make every rule opt-in. Toolkit adoption keeps the
default; changing a switch is an explicit project policy decision.

Enable mutation contracts explicitly with `toolkit.mutation.enabled: true`.

## Redundant PHPStan Diagnostics

The toolkit suppresses a PHPStan or Strict Rules diagnostic only when an enabled
toolkit rule makes that diagnostic non-actionable. The toolkit error remains as
the single instruction for fixing the prohibited construct:

| Enabled toolkit rule | Suppressed diagnostic | Scope |
|----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| `noNonPublicMethod` | `method.unused`, `method.finalPrivate` | Private method declarations; PHPStan does not emit either for constructors, and `consistentConstructor.private` stays visible because the rule exempts constructors |
| `noPrivateMethodInTestClass` | The same private-method diagnostics | Restricted test classes |
| `noPropertyInTestClass` | `property.unused`, `property.neverRead`, `property.neverWritten`, `property.onlyRead`, `property.onlyWritten` | Restricted test classes |
| `noClassConstantInTestClass` | `classConstant.unused` | Restricted test classes |
| `noControlFlowInTestMethod` | PHPStan and Strict Rules diagnostics emitted for the prohibited `if`, loop, `switch`, or `match` node | Test methods in restricted test classes |
| `requireThrowsTagOnDirectThrow` | `missingType.checkedException` | Direct escaping throws in methods; propagated checked exceptions remain reported |

This is semantic suppression through PHPStan's extension API, not a global
`ignoreErrors` entry. Disabling the dominating toolkit rule automatically
restores the corresponding PHPStan diagnostics. Independent findings remain
visible; for example, an unused private property in production code and a dead
broad catch are still reported.

# AGENTS

## This Project

This project builds a complete Zero Table Dependency (ZTD) implementation for PHP.

ZTD runs tests on a real database engine without ever touching a physical table. Before a query reaches the database, every table it references is replaced by a CTE holding fixture rows (CTE shadowing), and every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE is turned into a SELECT that returns the rows the write would produce (result select query). Those rows are kept in the session, so later queries see the writes. One empty schema serves every test: no migrations, no seeding, no cleanup, and tests run in parallel without interfering.

The hard part is "complete". A rewrite must keep the meaning of whatever SQL the application sends, in every dialect and version, and a rewrite that is slightly wrong does not fail: it silently returns wrong test results. Hand-picked test cases cannot establish that. ZTD has to understand SQL exactly as the server does, and its behavior has to be checked against the server itself.

That is why the repository holds so many packages. The `ztd-query-*` packages are the product, split only so that users install the dialect and driver they need. Everything else exists for quality, and it is the core of this project: reading the official grammars instead of approximating them, parsing and binding SQL the way the server does, generating every statement form the grammars allow, running the statements against the real servers and comparing the results, and tracing each specification back to the manual it comes from. Correctness comes from that machinery, not from examples.

The repository is also an experiment in how AI agents can build something this complex correctly, so every claim about behavior has to be backed by tests, fuzzing, or a specification.

## Supported Versions

### ZTD Query (ztd-query-*)

- PHP 8.1+
- MySQL 8.0–9.1
- PostgreSQL 16–17
- SQLite 3.x

### Other packages

- PHP 8.1+
- MySQL 5.6–9.1
- PostgreSQL 16–17
- SQLite 3.x

An AI agent that is asked to make a test pass will also lengthen a method, add a `Helper` class, open a new section in the README or lower the PHPStan level, if nothing stops it. Each of those changes looks reasonable alone. Guard declares what the project has decided about them in `guard.yaml`, reports every change that departs from it, and repairs the departures that have exactly one correct fix.

## Policies

| Section | What it checks | Rule IDs | Repaired by `fix` |
|---------|----------------|----------|---------------------|
| `metrics` | Lines and cyclomatic complexity of PHP files, classes, functions and methods. See [metrics](metrics.md). | `metrics.*` | no |
| `structure` | What each directory may contain, how entries are named, and how many there are. See [structure](structure.md). | `structure.*` | no |
| `documentation` | The headings, outline, badges or exact content of Markdown files, and Markdown files nobody declared. See [documents](documents.md). | `documentation.*` | no |
| `configuration` | Values in the configuration files of other tools, such as `phpstan.neon` or `phpunit.xml.dist`. See [configuration fields](fields.md). | the rule's `id` | yes, when the rule has a repair |
| `test_dependencies` | Composer development namespaces and Deptrac dependency boundaries for test directories. See [test dependencies](fields.md#test-dependencies). | `test-dependencies.*` | yes, including a missing Deptrac file |
| `benchmarks` | PHPBench directory contents, filenames, namespace references and Composer commands. See [benchmarks](benchmarks.md). | `phpbench.*` | Composer fields only |
| `extensions` | Whatever a project or a package adds. See [extensions](extensions.md). | chosen by the extension | when the extension proposes a change |

A section that `guard.yaml` neither writes nor [imports](configuration.md#imports) is not checked.

## Required and recommended

Every finding is either required or recommended. A required finding is reported as `error` and fails the command with exit code `1`. A recommendation is reported as `warning` and leaves the exit code at `0`. Configuration rules choose their level with `level`; metric, structure and document findings are always required.

## What is repaired

`guard fix` only writes configuration fields. A field has one value that satisfies its rule, or a declared fallback, so writing it is a deterministic edit. Splitting a method, renaming a class or rewriting a section is not, so those findings remain until someone edits the code or the document.

Each message names the offending file and symbol, what the policy expects, and how to comply. It also says that changing the declaration itself needs a human to update `guard.yaml`, so an agent fixes the project instead of the policy.

## Workflow

1. Run `guard init` to write a `guard.yaml` that imports the presets matching the project. See [init](cli.md#init).
2. Review the file, adjust thresholds and declarations in the [configuration](configuration.md), and commit it.
3. Run `guard fix --dry-run`, then `guard fix`, to bring the tool configuration in line.
4. Fix the remaining findings in code and documents until `guard check` passes.
5. Run `guard check` in CI. When a finding reflects a deliberate decision, a human changes `guard.yaml` in the same change.

## What it does not prove

Guard checks shape: sizes, names, headings and values. A short method can still be wrong, and a README with the declared sections can still be out of date. Passing `guard check` means the project has not drifted from what was decided, not that the decisions are good.
# Configuration

`guard.yaml` declares the policies of a project. Commands read `guard.yaml` in the working directory; pass `--config FILE` to use another. Every path in it is relative to the directory of the main `guard.yaml`, whatever the working directory and wherever an import lives.

## Example

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/metrics.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/structure.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/phpstan.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/readme-md.yaml
metrics:
  source: [src]
  profiles:
    standard:
      limits:

documentation:
```

| Key | Required | Description |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| `version` | yes | Always `1`. An imported file may omit it. |
| `imports` | no | Other policy files to load first. See [Imports](#imports). |
| `collect` | no | The files Guard may read at all. See [Collection scope](#collection-scope). |
| `metrics` | no | PHP size and complexity limits. See [metrics](metrics.md). |
| `structure` | no | Directory rules. See [structure](structure.md). |

Unknown keys, invalid types, contradictory bounds and two `configuration` rules with the same `id` in one file are errors with exit code `2`. Error messages name a section by the file it came from historically, such as `tree.yaml` for `structure` or `doc-guard.yaml` for `documentation`.

## Imports

Each entry of `imports` is a path relative to the file that lists it, or an absolute path. An imported file may import more files. Guard loads the imports in order and then applies the file itself, so a later import overrides an earlier one and the project file overrides all of them. A circular import is an error.

An override keeps every imported value it does not mention:

| Key | Merged by |
|-----|-----------|
| `collect.include`, `collect.exclude` | Each list replaces the imported one when set. |
| `metrics.profiles` | Profile name. A profile replaces only the keys it sets, and inside `limits` only the metrics it sets. |
| `metrics.source`, `metrics.exclude`, `metrics.default`, `metrics.assignments` | Each replaces the imported value when set. |
| `structure.directories` | `path`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new path is added. |
| `structure.paths`, `structure.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |
| `documentation.files` | Document path. A declaration replaces only the keys it sets, so a project can add `headings` to a document whose `outlines` come from a preset. |
| `documentation.scan`, `documentation.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |
| `configuration` | `id`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new `id` is added. |
| `test_dependencies` | The whole settings mapping is replaced; omitted settings use their defaults. |
| `benchmarks` | The boolean is replaced. `false` disables an imported benchmark policy. |
| `extensions` | Class name. A later declaration replaces that class's whole option mapping and keeps its position. |

To drop an imported rule, remove the import and write the rules you want in the project file instead. A policy without `imports` is a complete custom policy.

## Collection scope

`collect` limits which files Guard reads. Every policy, built-in or from an extension, sees only what lies inside it:

```text
files a policy sees = (collect.include − collect.exclude) ∩ files the policy asks for
```

```yaml
version: 1
collect:
  include: [src, docs, README.md, schemas/catalog.xsd]
  exclude: ['**/generated/**', 'docs/archive/**']
```

| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `include` | `['**']` | Paths and globs to read. A directory includes everything below it. `[]` selects nothing. |
| `exclude` | `[]` | Paths and globs removed from `include`. An excluded directory is skipped with everything below it. |

`*` matches within one path segment and `**` matches any number of segments. Absolute paths, `..` and backslashes are rejected. Symbolic links are not followed.

When `collect` is set, it replaces the per-section reading scopes `metrics.source` and `metrics.exclude`, `structure.paths` and `structure.exclude`, and `documentation.exclude`, including values from presets. Metrics then read every `.php` file in the scope. Assignments, directory rule paths, declared documents, scan patterns and configuration rule files still choose what each policy checks.

A file outside the scope is treated as if a policy had not asked for it: a declared document or configuration file outside the scope is skipped, not reported as missing. Without `collect`, each section keeps its own scope settings.

Guard walks the file system once for all policies, reads each file at most once and parses it at most once per format, however many policies ask for it.

## Enabling and Disabling Rules

Rules inherit `toolkit.allRules`, which defaults to `true`, except mutation
contracts, which are opt-in so an existing unannotated project does not change
semantics on upgrade. Override a specific rule through its `enabled` value:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        forbidEmptyCatch:
            enabled: false
```

Set `allRules: false` to make every rule opt-in. Toolkit adoption keeps the
default; changing a switch is an explicit project policy decision.

Enable mutation contracts explicitly with `toolkit.mutation.enabled: true`.

## Redundant PHPStan Diagnostics

The toolkit suppresses a PHPStan or Strict Rules diagnostic only when an enabled
toolkit rule makes that diagnostic non-actionable. The toolkit error remains as
the single instruction for fixing the prohibited construct:

| Enabled toolkit rule | Suppressed diagnostic | Scope |
|----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| `noNonPublicMethod` | `method.unused`, `method.finalPrivate` | Private method declarations; PHPStan does not emit either for constructors, and `consistentConstructor.private` stays visible because the rule exempts constructors |
| `noPrivateMethodInTestClass` | The same private-method diagnostics | Restricted test classes |
| `noPropertyInTestClass` | `property.unused`, `property.neverRead`, `property.neverWritten`, `property.onlyRead`, `property.onlyWritten` | Restricted test classes |
| `noClassConstantInTestClass` | `classConstant.unused` | Restricted test classes |
| `noControlFlowInTestMethod` | PHPStan and Strict Rules diagnostics emitted for the prohibited `if`, loop, `switch`, or `match` node | Test methods in restricted test classes |
| `requireThrowsTagOnDirectThrow` | `missingType.checkedException` | Direct escaping throws in methods; propagated checked exceptions remain reported |

This is semantic suppression through PHPStan's extension API, not a global
`ignoreErrors` entry. Disabling the dominating toolkit rule automatically
restores the corresponding PHPStan diagnostics. Independent findings remain
visible; for example, an unused private property in production code and a dead
broad catch are still reported.

# AGENTS

## This Project

This project builds a complete Zero Table Dependency (ZTD) implementation for PHP.

ZTD runs tests on a real database engine without ever touching a physical table. Before a query reaches the database, every table it references is replaced by a CTE holding fixture rows (CTE shadowing), and every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE is turned into a SELECT that returns the rows the write would produce (result select query). Those rows are kept in the session, so later queries see the writes. One empty schema serves every test: no migrations, no seeding, no cleanup, and tests run in parallel without interfering.

The hard part is "complete". A rewrite must keep the meaning of whatever SQL the application sends, in every dialect and version, and a rewrite that is slightly wrong does not fail: it silently returns wrong test results. Hand-picked test cases cannot establish that. ZTD has to understand SQL exactly as the server does, and its behavior has to be checked against the server itself.

That is why the repository holds so many packages. The `ztd-query-*` packages are the product, split only so that users install the dialect and driver they need. Everything else exists for quality, and it is the core of this project: reading the official grammars instead of approximating them, parsing and binding SQL the way the server does, generating every statement form the grammars allow, running the statements against the real servers and comparing the results, and tracing each specification back to the manual it comes from. Correctness comes from that machinery, not from examples.

sql-fixture が切り替えるのに残っている課題
ブロッカー1: 宣言されていないテーブルへの外部キーで例外になる。 MySQL と PostgreSQL では、参照先のテーブルを依存として渡さないと、「No dependency declares the table」で失敗します。sql-fixture はテーブルを1つずつ読みます。このため、外部キーを持つテーブルの SHOW CREATE TABLE は必ず失敗します。単独の文字列を渡す FixtureProvider も、1ファイル1テーブルの DDL ディレクトリも同じです。SQLite はすでに受理しており、サーバーの挙動とも一致しています。MySQL と PostgreSQL でも、宣言を単独で読むときは、未解決の参照を例外ではなく「未解決」として記録する読み方が必要です。

ブロッカー2: リテラルを PHP の値に復号する手段がない。 ENUM と SET の値や DEFAULT は、綴りのままの型付き要素で返ります。sql-fixture は ENUM の値の中から1つを選んで生成するので、復号が必須です。Builder は PHP の値から SQL へ向かう方向を、sql_mode まで考慮して持っています。その逆方向も sql-semantics に置くべきです。そうしないと、sql-fixture が方言ごとの文字列リテラル復号器を持ち続けることになり、二重実装が残ります。

宣言	サーバー	sql-semantics
MySQL INT NOT NULL NULL	NULL 可。後から書いた方が勝つ	NOT NULL
MySQL INT SERIAL DEFAULT VALUE	NOT NULL、AUTO_INCREMENT、UNIQUE	NULL 可、自動採番なし
SQLite PRIMARY KEY (a + b, b)	拒否。主キーに式は使えない	受理。主キーを a, b として読む
SQLite CREATE TEMP TABLE	通常のテーブル	読めるテーブルなし

### R03：引数の「名前が同じ」ことを「値が変わっていない」と扱い、有限再帰を打ち切る

**該当箇所：**

`Evaluation/Candidate/Calls.php` の `expand()` / `unchangedArguments()`

例えば、

```php
function countDown($n)
{
    if ($n === 0) {
        return 0;
    }

    $n = $n - 1;

    return 1 + countDown($n);
}

function target()
{
    observe(countDown(4));
}
```

これは十分な展開深さがあれば、候補 `4` まで評価できる例です。

ところが `unchangedArguments()` は、実引数がローカル変数への参照で、その**変数名が同じ位置の仮引数名に一致するか**を見ています。引数の値や、その間の再代入は比較していません。`expand()` は、同じ呼び出し箇所が既に履歴にあり、この判定が真なら `CYCLE` を返します。

上のコードでは、実引数の表記は毎回 `$n` ですが、値は `4 → 3 → 2 → 1 → 0` と変わります。**現在の判定は、これを「引数不変の再帰」と誤認する条件になっています。**

既存の有限再帰テストは、

```php
return $n + total($n - 1);
```

という形です。この形では実引数が単純なローカル変数参照ではないため、同じ判定に掛かりません。したがって、そのテストがあっても今回の問題は残ります。

**修正方針：** 循環判定は、名前の一致ではなく、値の由来・束縛・必要な文脈が同じ依存へ戻ったかで行うべきです。少なくとも、再代入を考慮しない `unchangedArguments()` を、値が不変である証明として使用してはいけません。

「変化していないと証明できない」場合は、通常の深さ・再帰予算に従って展開すればよく、早々に `CYCLE` と断定する必要はありません。

**該当箇所：**

`Evaluation/Candidate/Origins.php` の `property()`

これは、今回特に修正を優先したい箇所です。

通常の `Calls::expand()` は、先に `Models::graph()` を呼びます。この部分のオーバーライド優先は正しく変更されています。 

しかし、生成したオブジェクトのプロパティを調べる `Properties::allocated()` は、次のようにコンストラクタの**ソースグラフを直接取得**します。

```php

);
```

ここにはモデル選択がありません。そのグラフに対象プロパティへの書き込みが見つかると、本体展開数を増やし、ソースの `finalStorage()` を解析します。

例えば、

```php
class Box
{
    public string $table = 'ledger';

    public function __construct()
    {
        $this->table = 'source_only';
    }

    public function tableName()
    {
        return $this->table;
    }
}

function target()
{
    observe((new Box)->tableName());
}
```

ここで `Box::__construct` を、**何も書き換えないモデル**で置き換えたとします。

期待する動作は、

```text
コンストラクタのソース本体を展開しない
    → 宣言時の "ledger" が残る
```

です。

ところが現行コードには、

```text
new Box の依存でモデルを選択
    ↓
tableName() からプロパティを要求
    ↓
Properties::allocated()
    ↓
元の Box::__construct のソースを直接取得
    ↓
"source_only" の書き込みを解析
```

という経路があります。**直接の呼び出しではオーバーライドしていても、プロパティの由来を通じて、置き換えたはずの本体へ再入場できます。** 

また、一般のプロパティ由来を集める `Origins::property()` も、`Index::writes()` で見つけたソースの代入右辺へ直接進みます。こちらについても、置換済みメソッドのソース書き込みを候補として拾ってよいのか、モデルとの一貫性が必要です。

**修正方針：** オーバーライドを「関数の戻り値を調べる入口だけの処理」にしないことです。

戻り値、参照引数への書き込み、オブジェクトのプロパティ初期化、モデル状態など、**どの依存から入っても、同じソース／モデル選択を経由する構造**にする必要があります。モデルで置き換えた本体は、別の依存経路からも展開されないことを保証すべきです。

| 共通 | **Lexer**：`my_sql_parser_lex()` | SQL文字列を保持する`Lex_input_stream` | token番号＋semantic value（`MY_SQL_PARSER_STYPE`）＋位置（`POS`）。 |
| SELECT / CREATE TABLE | **Parser**：`my_sql_parser_parse()` | Lexerから供給されるtoken列 | `Parse_tree_root*`。具体的には、SELECTなら **`PT_select_stmt`**、CREATE TABLEなら **`PT_create_table_stmt`**。 |
| SELECT | **Contextualization**：`PT_select_stmt::make_cmd()`、`contextualize()` | `PT_select_stmt`と配下のparse-tree nodes | **`Sql_cmd_select`**を生成。`LEX`に関連付けられた **`Query_expression`・`Query_block`・`Item`**などを構築・設定する。 |
| SELECT | **Resolving / prepare**：`Query_expression::prepare()`、`Query_block::prepare()` | `Query_expression`・`Query_block`・`Item` | **同じ構造を更新**。テーブル・列・式の解決や各種変換を反映する。別型の「解析済みAST」を一律に生成するわけではない。 |
| SELECT | **Optimization**：`Query_expression::optimize()` | prepareされた`Query_expression` | **`AccessPath`の木**。 |
| SELECT | `CreateIteratorFromAccessPath()` | `AccessPath`の木 | **`RowIterator`の木**。 |
| SELECT | **Execution**：`ExecuteIteratorQuery()`、iteratorの`Init()` / `Read()` | `RowIterator`の木 | 行を取得・処理し、**`Query_result`**へ渡す。 |
| SET | **Parser内のcontextualization**：`PT_set::contextualize()` | token列から作った **`PT_set`** | **`LEX::var_list`**（`List<set_var_base>`）と`SQLCOM_SET_OPTION`を設定。処理は文法アクション内で行われ、外へ返すrootは`nullptr`。 |
| SET | `sql_set_variables()` | `LEX::var_list`の`set_var`など | `resolve()` → `check()` → `update()`を行い、**変数の値を更新**する。 |
| CREATE TABLE | **Contextualization**：`PT_create_table_stmt::make_cmd()` | `PT_create_table_stmt` | **`Sql_cmd_create_table`**と、テーブル定義を保持する **`HA_CREATE_INFO`・`Alter_info`**。 |
| CREATE TABLE | `Sql_cmd_create_table::execute()` → `mysql_create_table()` | `Sql_cmd_create_table`、`HA_CREATE_INFO`、`Alter_info`など | **テーブルを作成**する。SELECT用の`AccessPath` → `RowIterator`の経路ではない。 |

上記はざっくりと調査をまとめたものになります。sql-parserがあるのでparserはそれを利用してください。sql-semanticsはResolvingに対応します。なのでparser -> semanticsの順に呼び出してください。semanticsのI/Fは変えてOkです。
またその後は実行に不要そうなところは外していいです。Optimatzationとかは特に不要な認識です。ただPathを作るIteratorを作るなどは欲しいです。

また接続はPDOで可能にしてください。話によるとmysqlndでそういうHookがあると聞いているのでそこで利用できるといいなと思っています。

最後に注意点としてMySQL実装を読んでPHPコードに落とすことはしないでください。あくまでもクリーンなオンメモリエミュレーターでありPHP再実装ではないです。なので概念はあとのために合わせたいがコードを模倣したいわけではないです。

# Configuration Fields

The `configuration` section checks single values in the configuration files of other tools: the PHPStan level, a PHPUnit attribute, a Composer setting. An agent that cannot make a check pass can lower that check instead; a field rule turns such an edit into a failure. Rules that know the correct value repair it with `guard fix`.

## Example

```yaml
version: 1
configuration:
  - id: phpstan.level
    file: phpstan.neon
    select: /parameters/level
    assert: {equals: max}
  - id: composer.sort-packages
    file: composer.json
    select: /config/sort-packages
    level: recommended
    assert: {equals: true}
  - id: phpunit.fail-on-warning
    file: phpunit.xml.dist
    format: xml
    select: /phpunit/@failOnWarning
    assert: {equals: 'true'}
  - id: infection.min-msi
    file: infection.json5
    select: /minMsi
    assert: {min: 80}
```

`guard fix` sets the PHPStan level to `max`, `sort-packages` to `true` and `failOnWarning` to `"true"`. The `minMsi` rule needs an explicit `repair: 80`, because `min` permits many values and does not choose one. Until that required rule is satisfied, `fix` writes none of the other repairs either. See [Repairs](#repairs).

## Fields

| Key | Required | Description |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| `id` | yes | Unique rule ID. Reported as the rule of each finding, and used to [override](configuration.md#imports) an imported rule. |
| `file` | yes | The configuration file, relative to `guard.yaml`. |
| `select` | yes | The field: a JSON Pointer, or an XPath for XML. See [Formats](#formats). |
| `assert` | yes | One or more [assertions](#assertions). All must hold. |
| `format` | no | `json`, `yaml`, `yml`, `neon`, `toml`, `xml`, `json5` or `php`. Default: the file extension. Set it for names such as `phpunit.xml.dist`. |
| `level` | no | `required` (default) fails the check; `recommended` warns. |
| `message` | no | Diagnostic describing the problem and the edit that resolves it. Supports `{file}`, `{select}`, `{expectation}` and `{fix}` placeholders. |
| `repair` | no | The value `fix` writes when the field is wrong. See [Repairs](#repairs). |

A target file that does not exist is reported at the rule's level and names the field it should contain. A file outside the [collection scope](configuration.md#collection-scope) is skipped.

## Assertions

| Assertion | Holds when |
|-----------|------------|
| `equals: V` | The value equals `V`, including its type: `1`, `'1'` and `true` differ, and so do a list and a mapping. Mapping key order is ignored. |
| `one_of: [A, B]` | The value equals one of the listed values. |
| `min: N`, `max: N` | The value is a number within the bound, which is included. |
| `contains: S` | A string contains `S`, or a list or mapping contains such a string at any depth. `key=value` also matches a mapping entry with that key and string value. |
| `contains_any: [A, B]` | A string or a list entry at any depth equals one of the names. A name with `/` also matches as part of an entry, such as an include path. |
| `not_contains: S` | `contains: S` does not hold. |
| `present: true` | The field exists. |
| `absent: true` | The field does not exist. It cannot be combined with another assertion. |

A missing field fails every assertion except `absent`, even `equals: null`: an explicit `null` and a missing key are different.

## Formats

| Format | `select` | Notes |
|--------|----------|-------|
| `json` | JSON Pointer, such as `/config/sort-packages` | Lists and objects, and scalar types, are kept apart. |
| `yaml`, `yml` | JSON Pointer | Parsed with Symfony YAML. Custom tags are rejected. |
| `neon` | JSON Pointer | Parsed with Nette NEON. |
| `toml` | JSON Pointer | TOML 0.4 syntax. Newer syntax fails without writing. TOML has no `null`. |
| `xml` | XPath that selects one element or attribute | Values are strings, so quote booleans and numbers in YAML; `min` and `max` still read numeric text. Use `local-name()` and `namespace-uri()` for namespaced documents. DTDs and entity declarations are rejected. |
| `json5` | JSON Pointer | Quoted keys, comments and trailing commas are accepted. Repairs serialize valid JSON, which is also valid JSON5. |
| `php` | JSON Pointer | A returned literal array, or `/riskyAllowed` and `/rules/<rule>` for PHP-CS-Fixer fluent configuration. Repairs replace the selected literal argument or returned array and can add missing setter calls. The file is never executed; ambiguous calls and dynamic values are errors when their value cannot be determined. |

In a JSON Pointer, `/` inside a key is written `~1` and `~` is written `~0`. A pointer into a list addresses an existing index or its next index, so `/includes/0` can create the first entry. Missing parents are created as maps, or lists when the next segment is a numeric index. Guard does not create gaps in lists or replace scalar parents with containers. An XPath that matches several nodes is an error.

A rule may include a non-empty `message` describing the problem and the required edit. Guard displays the same diagnostic in `rules`, `check` and remaining `fix` findings, with placeholders resolved after imports and overrides. If omitted, Guard generates a concrete diagnostic from the assertions. See [Rule messages](cli.md#rule-messages).

## Repairs

`equals` is its own repair. Every other assertion needs an explicit `repair` before `fix` can change the field, and the repair must satisfy all assertions of the rule:

```yaml
- id: application.driver
  file: settings.yaml
  select: /driver
  assert: {one_of: [mysql, pgsql]}
  repair: mysql
```

A field that already satisfies the rule is kept, so `pgsql` is not replaced by `mysql`. Without a repair, the finding stays and names the required change. Every supported format uses the same check-and-repair contract: select a field, write its repair value only when the assertion fails, then recheck the same assertions. Both levels are repaired.

Guard plans the changes to every file, then checks rules that touch the same file against the planned result. While a required rule stays unsatisfied, `fix` writes no file at all and reports the planned files as `blocked`. Missing fields and their parent containers are created along the selector. XML creation starts at the existing root and supports named elements, attribute-equality predicates such as `testsuite[@name="doctest"]`, and a final attribute such as `/@value`. XPath can still select existing values using more complex expressions; an ambiguous or indeterminate creation path is an error.

### Partial requirements and severity

`required` and `recommended` control whether a remaining violation fails the command; they do not change the matching condition. `equals` requires equality of the selected value. `one_of`, `contains`, presence checks, and separate rules for individual fields keep their existing meanings. A rule selecting one XML attribute does not require the whole element to match, and adding that attribute preserves custom attributes, sibling elements, and their values. A compliant value is never replaced by the repair's default.

### Enabling PHPUnit features

Import the presets for the PHPUnit major the project uses, then run `guard fix --dry-run` and `guard fix`:

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/phpunit13.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/doctest13.yaml
```

Starting with an existing `phpunit.xml.dist`, these rules can add the reporter extension, Doctest suite and extension, source-directory parameter, and PHPUnit settings. Existing suites and extension parameters are retained. A project created with [`guard init`](cli.md#init) also carries a `unit` and an `integration` suite rule for each of `tests/Unit` and `tests/Integration` that exists, and `fix` adds the missing suite. The Doctest suite repair points at `vendor/k-kinzal/doctest-php/`; the source-directory repair defaults to `src`. Override the corresponding rule's `repair` to choose another default; a directory value already present remains unchanged. Install the corresponding Composer packages before running PHPUnit. Guard configures their activation; it does not install dependencies.

### Writing

A file that does not change keeps every byte. A changed JSON, JSON5, YAML, NEON or TOML file is serialized again, so its indentation may change and its comments are lost; the result is parsed again and must hold the same data apart from the repaired fields. A changed XML file keeps unrelated nodes and comments. PHP repairs preserve statements outside the replaced literal; comments within that literal may be lost.

Guard writes each file to a temporary file in the same directory and replaces the original atomically, keeping its permissions, and refuses to write when the file changed since it was read. Each replacement is atomic, but a failure in the middle of several files can leave the earlier ones written; fix the cause and run `guard check` again.

Targets must be regular files inside the project. Paths that leave the project or pass through a symbolic link are rejected, and a rule cannot edit `guard.yaml` itself.

## Test dependencies

Import the dedicated preset to isolate the root `bench/`, `fuzz/`, `spec/`, and `tests/` directories:

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/test-dependencies.yaml
```

For a new policy, `guard init` selects this preset whenever any of those directories exists. To select only this policy, use `guard init --import=test-dependencies`. For an existing policy, add the import above. Then run:

```console
vendor/bin/guard check
vendor/bin/guard fix --dry-run
vendor/bin/guard fix
composer dump-autoload
composer deptrac
```

Each existing directory requires its own entry in `composer.json` under `autoload-dev.psr-4`: `Bench\: bench/`, `Fuzz\: fuzz/`, `Spec\: spec/`, and `Tests\: tests/`. Missing directories do not require mappings or new layers. Guard detects directories on every run, so adding `fuzz/` after initialization activates its checks automatically. The normal collection scope applies: include the test directories and both configuration files when using `collect`.

`fix` adds the directories and `src/` to Deptrac's analysis paths, configures class and standalone-file dependency analysis, and creates independent layers with namespace and directory collectors. Tests within one directory may refer to each other. References between different test directories and references from production code to a test directory are forbidden. Each test layer may depend on production layers only. Dependencies in PHP code are checked by `composer deptrac`; Guard checks that its configuration enforces these boundaries. The policy adds or repairs the Composer `deptrac` script to run the selected file.

By default, `Src` collects all production code under `src/`. Existing projects with more specific production layers can name them explicitly:

```yaml
test_dependencies:
  deptrac: deptrac.yml
  source_layers: [Domain, Application, Infrastructure]
```

`deptrac` must be a YAML filename in the project root; the default is `deptrac.yaml`. `source_layers` defaults to `[Src]`. Named custom layers must already have collectors. Guard confines those collectors to `src/`, retains their internal dependency rules, removes permissions to reference test layers (including `+Tests`), and lets each test layer refer to all named production layers. The reserved `Src` layer collects production code not matched by those custom layers, without overlapping them. Test layer collectors and their allowed destinations are managed by this policy; other layer settings are preserved.

The findings use `test-dependencies.autoload.<directory>` for each namespace mapping, and `test-dependencies.deptrac.*` for paths, layers, ruleset, analysis types, script and bypass checks. `guard rules --query=test-dependencies` lists the policy's capability without reading the target files.

The preset requires an existing `composer.json`. It can create a missing Deptrac YAML file; dry-run previews that file without creating it. As with other repairs, conflicting required rules block every write. Repeated successful repairs leave the files byte-identical. Install `deptrac/deptrac` separately before running its Composer script; Guard does not install packages.

Deptrac `exclude_files` is cleared so test dependencies cannot disappear from analysis. Baseline entries involving the four test namespaces are removed; unrelated entries remain. Non-empty Deptrac `imports` requires a manual change: inline those settings into the selected file before fixing, so Guard can check the complete ruleset. Guard reports that condition and writes nothing. Existing configurations using extensions that change Deptrac's analysis require their own review.

# Configuration Fields

The `configuration` section checks single values in the configuration files of other tools: the PHPStan level, a PHPUnit attribute, a Composer setting. An agent that cannot make a check pass can lower that check instead; a field rule turns such an edit into a failure. Rules that know the correct value repair it with `guard fix`.

## Example

```yaml
version: 1
configuration:
  - id: phpstan.level
    file: phpstan.neon
    select: /parameters/level
    assert: {equals: max}
  - id: composer.sort-packages
    file: composer.json
    select: /config/sort-packages
    level: recommended
    assert: {equals: true}
  - id: phpunit.fail-on-warning
    file: phpunit.xml.dist
    format: xml
    select: /phpunit/@failOnWarning
    assert: {equals: 'true'}
  - id: infection.min-msi
    file: infection.json5
    select: /minMsi
    assert: {min: 80}
```

`guard fix` sets the PHPStan level to `max`, `sort-packages` to `true` and `failOnWarning` to `"true"`. The `minMsi` rule needs an explicit `repair: 80`, because `min` permits many values and does not choose one. Until that required rule is satisfied, `fix` writes none of the other repairs either. See [Repairs](#repairs).

## Fields

| Key | Required | Description |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| `id` | yes | Unique rule ID. Reported as the rule of each finding, and used to [override](configuration.md#imports) an imported rule. |
| `file` | yes | The configuration file, relative to `guard.yaml`. |
| `select` | yes | The field: a JSON Pointer, or an XPath for XML. See [Formats](#formats). |
| `assert` | yes | One or more [assertions](#assertions). All must hold. |
| `format` | no | `json`, `yaml`, `yml`, `neon`, `toml`, `xml`, `json5` or `php`. Default: the file extension. Set it for names such as `phpunit.xml.dist`. |
| `level` | no | `required` (default) fails the check; `recommended` warns. |
| `message` | no | Diagnostic describing the problem and the edit that resolves it. Supports `{file}`, `{select}`, `{expectation}` and `{fix}` placeholders. |
| `repair` | no | The value `fix` writes when the field is wrong. See [Repairs](#repairs). |

A target file that does not exist is reported at the rule's level and names the field it should contain. A file outside the [collection scope](configuration.md#collection-scope) is skipped.

## Assertions

| Assertion | Holds when |
|-----------|------------|
| `equals: V` | The value equals `V`, including its type: `1`, `'1'` and `true` differ, and so do a list and a mapping. Mapping key order is ignored. |
| `one_of: [A, B]` | The value equals one of the listed values. |
| `min: N`, `max: N` | The value is a number within the bound, which is included. |
| `contains: S` | A string contains `S`, or a list or mapping contains such a string at any depth. `key=value` also matches a mapping entry with that key and string value. |
| `contains_any: [A, B]` | A string or a list entry at any depth equals one of the names. A name with `/` also matches as part of an entry, such as an include path. |
| `not_contains: S` | `contains: S` does not hold. |
| `present: true` | The field exists. |
| `absent: true` | The field does not exist. It cannot be combined with another assertion. |

A missing field fails every assertion except `absent`, even `equals: null`: an explicit `null` and a missing key are different.

## Formats

| Format | `select` | Notes |
|--------|----------|-------|
| `json` | JSON Pointer, such as `/config/sort-packages` | Lists and objects, and scalar types, are kept apart. |
| `yaml`, `yml` | JSON Pointer | Parsed with Symfony YAML. Custom tags are rejected. |
| `neon` | JSON Pointer | Parsed with Nette NEON. |
| `toml` | JSON Pointer | TOML 0.4 syntax. Newer syntax fails without writing. TOML has no `null`. |
| `xml` | XPath that selects one element or attribute | Values are strings, so quote booleans and numbers in YAML; `min` and `max` still read numeric text. Use `local-name()` and `namespace-uri()` for namespaced documents. DTDs and entity declarations are rejected. |
| `json5` | JSON Pointer | Quoted keys, comments and trailing commas are accepted. Repairs serialize valid JSON, which is also valid JSON5. |
| `php` | JSON Pointer | A returned literal array, or `/riskyAllowed` and `/rules/<rule>` for PHP-CS-Fixer fluent configuration. Repairs replace the selected literal argument or returned array and can add missing setter calls. The file is never executed; ambiguous calls and dynamic values are errors when their value cannot be determined. |

In a JSON Pointer, `/` inside a key is written `~1` and `~` is written `~0`. A pointer into a list addresses an existing index or its next index, so `/includes/0` can create the first entry. Missing parents are created as maps, or lists when the next segment is a numeric index. Guard does not create gaps in lists or replace scalar parents with containers. An XPath that matches several nodes is an error.

A rule may include a non-empty `message` describing the problem and the required edit. Guard displays the same diagnostic in `rules`, `check` and remaining `fix` findings, with placeholders resolved after imports and overrides. If omitted, Guard generates a concrete diagnostic from the assertions. See [Rule messages](cli.md#rule-messages).

## Repairs

`equals` is its own repair. Every other assertion needs an explicit `repair` before `fix` can change the field, and the repair must satisfy all assertions of the rule:

```yaml
- id: application.driver
  file: settings.yaml
  select: /driver
  assert: {one_of: [mysql, pgsql]}
  repair: mysql
```

A field that already satisfies the rule is kept, so `pgsql` is not replaced by `mysql`. Without a repair, the finding stays and names the required change. Every supported format uses the same check-and-repair contract: select a field, write its repair value only when the assertion fails, then recheck the same assertions. Both levels are repaired.

Guard plans the changes to every file, then checks rules that touch the same file against the planned result. While a required rule stays unsatisfied, `fix` writes no file at all and reports the planned files as `blocked`. Missing fields and their parent containers are created along the selector. XML creation starts at the existing root and supports named elements, attribute-equality predicates such as `testsuite[@name="doctest"]`, and a final attribute such as `/@value`. XPath can still select existing values using more complex expressions; an ambiguous or indeterminate creation path is an error.

### Partial requirements and severity

`required` and `recommended` control whether a remaining violation fails the command; they do not change the matching condition. `equals` requires equality of the selected value. `one_of`, `contains`, presence checks, and separate rules for individual fields keep their existing meanings. A rule selecting one XML attribute does not require the whole element to match, and adding that attribute preserves custom attributes, sibling elements, and their values. A compliant value is never replaced by the repair's default.

### Enabling PHPUnit features

Import the presets for the PHPUnit major the project uses, then run `guard fix --dry-run` and `guard fix`:

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/phpunit13.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/doctest13.yaml
```

Starting with an existing `phpunit.xml.dist`, these rules can add the reporter extension, Doctest suite and extension, source-directory parameter, and PHPUnit settings. Existing suites and extension parameters are retained. A project created with [`guard init`](cli.md#init) also carries a `unit` and an `integration` suite rule for each of `tests/Unit` and `tests/Integration` that exists, and `fix` adds the missing suite. The Doctest suite repair points at `vendor/k-kinzal/doctest-php/`; the source-directory repair defaults to `src`. Override the corresponding rule's `repair` to choose another default; a directory value already present remains unchanged. Install the corresponding Composer packages before running PHPUnit. Guard configures their activation; it does not install dependencies.

### Writing

A file that does not change keeps every byte. A changed JSON, JSON5, YAML, NEON or TOML file is serialized again, so its indentation may change and its comments are lost; the result is parsed again and must hold the same data apart from the repaired fields. A changed XML file keeps unrelated nodes and comments. PHP repairs preserve statements outside the replaced literal; comments within that literal may be lost.

Guard writes each file to a temporary file in the same directory and replaces the original atomically, keeping its permissions, and refuses to write when the file changed since it was read. Each replacement is atomic, but a failure in the middle of several files can leave the earlier ones written; fix the cause and run `guard check` again.

Targets must be regular files inside the project. Paths that leave the project or pass through a symbolic link are rejected, and a rule cannot edit `guard.yaml` itself.

## Test dependencies

Import the dedicated preset to isolate the root `bench/`, `fuzz/`, `spec/`, and `tests/` directories:

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/test-dependencies.yaml
```

For a new policy, `guard init` selects this preset whenever any of those directories exists. To select only this policy, use `guard init --import=test-dependencies`. For an existing policy, add the import above. Then run:

```console
vendor/bin/guard check
vendor/bin/guard fix --dry-run
vendor/bin/guard fix
composer dump-autoload
composer deptrac
```

Each existing directory requires its own entry in `composer.json` under `autoload-dev.psr-4`: `Bench\: bench/`, `Fuzz\: fuzz/`, `Spec\: spec/`, and `Tests\: tests/`. Missing directories do not require mappings or new layers. Guard detects directories on every run, so adding `fuzz/` after initialization activates its checks automatically. The normal collection scope applies: include the test directories and both configuration files when using `collect`.

`fix` adds the directories and `src/` to Deptrac's analysis paths, configures class and standalone-file dependency analysis, and creates independent layers with namespace and directory collectors. Tests within one directory may refer to each other. References between different test directories and references from production code to a test directory are forbidden. Each test layer may depend on production layers only. Dependencies in PHP code are checked by `composer deptrac`; Guard checks that its configuration enforces these boundaries. The policy adds or repairs the Composer `deptrac` script to run the selected file.

By default, `Src` collects all production code under `src/`. Existing projects with more specific production layers can name them explicitly:

```yaml
test_dependencies:
  deptrac: deptrac.yml
  source_layers: [Domain, Application, Infrastructure]
```

`deptrac` must be a YAML filename in the project root; the default is `deptrac.yaml`. `source_layers` defaults to `[Src]`. Named custom layers must already have collectors. Guard confines those collectors to `src/`, retains their internal dependency rules, removes permissions to reference test layers (including `+Tests`), and lets each test layer refer to all named production layers. The reserved `Src` layer collects production code not matched by those custom layers, without overlapping them. Test layer collectors and their allowed destinations are managed by this policy; other layer settings are preserved.

The findings use `test-dependencies.autoload.<directory>` for each namespace mapping, and `test-dependencies.deptrac.*` for paths, layers, ruleset, analysis types, script and bypass checks. `guard rules --query=test-dependencies` lists the policy's capability without reading the target files.

The preset requires an existing `composer.json`. It can create a missing Deptrac YAML file; dry-run previews that file without creating it. As with other repairs, conflicting required rules block every write. Repeated successful repairs leave the files byte-identical. Install `deptrac/deptrac` separately before running its Composer script; Guard does not install packages.

Deptrac `exclude_files` is cleared so test dependencies cannot disappear from analysis. Baseline entries involving the four test namespaces are removed; unrelated entries remain. Non-empty Deptrac `imports` requires a manual change: inline those settings into the selected file before fixing, so Guard can check the complete ruleset. Guard reports that condition and writes nothing. Existing configurations using extensions that change Deptrac's analysis require their own review.

# RequireClassPairRule

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Identifiers | `customRules.classPairMissing`, `customRules.classPairOrphaned` |
| Scope | Every named class, interface, trait, and enum declaration in the analyzed paths |
| Rector | Unavailable |
| Configurable | Yes (`classPairs`, `classPairExclude`, `classPairProjectRoot`) |

## What It Detects

A class pair declares that when a class matching one name template exists, a class matching a second template must exist too. The shipped pair requires a unit test class for every production class:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        classPairs:
            -
                from: '${src}\{name}'
                to: '${tests/Unit}\{name}Test'
```

`${src}` and `${tests/Unit}` are read from the PSR-4 sections of `composer.json`. With `"App\\": "src/"` under `autoload` and `"Tests\\": "tests/"` under `autoload-dev`, the pair becomes `App\{name}` and `Tests\Unit\{name}Test`. `{name}` stands for the rest of the class name, including nested namespaces, so `App\Service\UserService` needs `Tests\Unit\Service\UserServiceTest`.

### 1. Class without its counterpart (`customRules.classPairMissing`)

```
src/Service/UserService.php      <-- ERROR: no Tests\Unit\Service\UserServiceTest
src/Service/OrderService.php     <-- OK
tests/Unit/Service/OrderServiceTest.php
```

```
Create class "Tests\Unit\Service\UserServiceTest" in tests/Unit/Service/UserServiceTest.php
for class "App\Service\UserService": every class matching "App\{name}" needs a class
matching "Tests\Unit\{name}Test".
```

### 2. Counterpart without its origin (`customRules.classPairOrphaned`)

```
src/Service/OrderService.php
tests/Unit/Service/OrderServiceTest.php    <-- OK
tests/Unit/Service/LegacyServiceTest.php   <-- ERROR: no App\Service\LegacyService
```

```
Create class "App\Service\LegacyService" in src/Service/LegacyService.php for class
"Tests\Unit\Service\LegacyServiceTest", or remove "Tests\Unit\Service\LegacyServiceTest":
every class matching "Tests\Unit\{name}Test" needs a class matching "App\{name}".
```

The file in the message is where PSR-4 expects the missing class. It is omitted when no `composer.json` entry covers the namespace.

## Why This Is an Error

### Missing counterparts

Every production class should have a unit test that pins its behavior. AI code generators often create production code without tests, or create tests for some classes but not others. Declaring the pair makes the gap visible at analysis time rather than during code review, and the same mechanism can require a fake for every interface or a factory for every entity.

### Orphaned counterparts

When a class is renamed or deleted, its test may be left behind. Orphaned tests waste CI time, inflate coverage, and mislead the next reader about which classes exist.

## How to Fix

### For a missing counterpart

Create the class named in the message at the file named in the message:

```php
// tests/Unit/Service/UserServiceTest.php
namespace Tests\Unit\Service;

use App\Service\UserService;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testCreatePersistsUser(): void
    {
        // ...
    }
}
```

### For an orphaned counterpart

Either delete the stale class or rename it to match the current origin:

```bash
# If the origin was renamed
git mv tests/Unit/Service/LegacyServiceTest.php tests/Unit/Service/ModernServiceTest.php

# If the origin was deleted
git rm tests/Unit/Service/LegacyServiceTest.php
```

## Configuration

### Templates

`from` and `to` are fully qualified class name templates. Each contains one `{name}` placeholder; text before it is a required prefix and text after it a required suffix. A template without `{name}` is a namespace prefix, so `from: '${src}'` means `${src}\{name}`. Matching is case-sensitive and `{name}` only matches valid class name segments, so `Tests\Unit\Test` never matches `Tests\Unit\{name}Test`.

Each pair is checked in both directions: a class matching `from` needs the class produced by `to`, and a class matching `to` needs the class produced by `from`. Pairs whose two templates produce the same class name for a class are ignored.

### Placeholders from `composer.json`

`${directory}` is replaced with the namespace that the `autoload` or `autoload-dev` PSR-4 section maps to that root-relative directory. A subdirectory of a mapped directory receives the mapped namespace plus one segment per path component, which is how `${tests/Unit}` resolves to `Tests\Unit`. The longest mapped directory wins. The `composer.json` is read from `classPairProjectRoot`, which defaults to `%currentWorkingDirectory%`; set it when PHPStan runs from another directory:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        classPairProjectRoot: %rootDir%/../../..
```

A pair whose placeholder names a directory without a PSR-4 mapping is skipped, so the shipped default is inert in a project without a `src/` namespace. Write the namespaces literally when the project autoloads through a classmap.

### Adding pairs

PHPStan merges lists, so a project adds pairs without repeating the default:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        classPairs:
            -
                from: '${src}\{name}Interface'
                to: '${src}\Fake\Fake{name}'
            -
                from: '${src}\Entity\{name}'
                to: '${tests/Unit}\Entity\{name}FactoryTest'
```

Use `classPairs!:` to replace the whole list, or `classPairs!: []` to keep the rule enabled with no pairs.

### Excluding classes

`classPairExclude` lists class name globs that no pair checks, in either direction. `*` matches any text including namespace separators, `?` matches one character, and `${directory}` placeholders are expanded. Because PHPStan merges lists, this is how a project exempts classes from the shipped pair without restating it:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        classPairExclude:
            - '${src}\Generated\*'
            - '*Interface'
            - '${tests/Unit}\Compatibility\ClassAliasesTest'
```

A pair's own `exclude` list applies to that pair only:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        classPairs:
            -
                from: '${src}\{name}Interface'
                to: '${src}\Fake\Fake{name}'
                exclude:
                    - '${src}\Legacy\*'
```

A test class that covers a file without a class, or a second test class declared in an existing test file, has no origin and is reported as orphaned. Exclude it by name when it is deliberate.

### Disabling

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        classPair:
            enabled: false
```

## Rector

**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.

A meaningful counterpart carries behavior of its own. Generating an empty class would only hide the violation.
# PropertyTestConventionRule

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Identifiers | `customRules.propertyTestLocation`, `customRules.propertyTestClassName`, `customRules.propertyTestExtends`, `customRules.propertyTestMethodName`, `customRules.propertyTestMethodSignature`, `customRules.propertyTestDiscovery` |
| Scope | Classes under `tests/Property`, in `Tests\Property`, or PHPUnit subclasses named `*Properties` or using `Eris\TestTrait` |
| Rector | Unavailable |
| Configuration | `toolkit.propertyTestConvention.enabled` (inherits `allRules`) |

## What it checks

Property tests belong under `tests/Property`, with a class named `<Name>Properties` extending `PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase` directly. Guard's `pbt` preset restricts their filenames to `*Properties.php`.

Every method declared in the class must be named `satisfies<PropertyName>`, with an uppercase letter after `satisfies`. The method must be public, concrete, non-static, and have no parameters. Generate inputs inside the method. Helpers, constructors, lifecycle overrides such as `setUp`, and data providers cannot be declared in a property test class.

Mark each method with PHPUnit's `#[Test]` attribute so it runs despite not starting with `test`. Projects using PHPUnit 9 must use `@test`; projects supporting both versions can carry both markers. The rule requires the attribute when PHPUnit 10+ is installed and accepts the annotation on PHPUnit 9.

```php
<?php

namespace Tests\Property;

use Eris\Generators;
use Eris\TestTrait;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Test;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class IntegerProperties extends TestCase
{
    use TestTrait;

    #[Test]
    public function satisfiesAdditionIdentity(): void
    {
        $this->forAll(Generators::int())->then(function (int $value): void {
            self::assertSame($value, $value + 0);
        });
    }
}
```

## Shared test rules

Property tests also receive the existing restrictions on declared properties, class constants, private methods, helper traits, Reflection, broken-code expectations, redundant assertions, and control flow in test methods. The control-flow rule keeps its existing boundary: nested closures and anonymous classes are separate scopes. `Tests\Property` is included in the default restricted namespaces for descriptive PHPDoc and public API documentation rules.

`Eris\TestTrait` is allowed without trait adaptations because it supplies the PBT framework. Other traits remain prohibited. PHPUnit mock API restrictions do not apply to property tests, including concrete-class mocks. The Unit naming and source/test pairing conventions are not imposed on property test methods; property tests do not replace Unit test coverage requirements.

## Guard configuration

Import `vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/pbt.yaml`, alongside the project's PHPUnit and PHPStan presets. `guard init` selects it automatically when `giorgiosironi/eris` is installed. The preset requires Composer scripts containing `--testsuite=unit` for `test:unit` and `--testsuite=property` for `test:pbt`.

For each selected PHPUnit preset, `guard init` adds a property suite requirement when `tests/Property` exists or the `pbt` preset is selected. It also requires the discovery suffix:

```xml
<testsuite name="property">
    <directory suffix="Properties.php">tests/Property</directory>
</testsuite>
```

Existing Guard configurations must add these suite requirements when adopting PBT; importing `pbt.yaml` alone does not regenerate project-specific PHPUnit rules. Keep `tests/Property` in PHPStan's analysis paths.

## Rector

No automatic rewrite is provided: the property name and the move of setup behavior require a test author to choose the intended semantics.
# EnforceVisibilityScopeRule

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Identifiers | `customRules.visibilityInvalidScope`, `customRules.visibilityOutOfScope` |
| Scope | Class-like declarations, members, and written class-like references in PHPStan's analysed files |
| Rector | Unavailable |
| Configurable | Yes |

## Purpose

PHP exports every namespace declaration to the whole program. `@visibility` adds the namespace scopes that PHP's
language visibility cannot express, corresponding to Rust's `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, and `pub(in path)`. PHPStan
collects declarations and written references from the files it already analyses, then reports a reference made from
outside the declaration's scope.

```php
namespace App\Billing\Ledger;

/**
 * Appends entries to the ledger file.
 *
 * @visibility parent
 */
final class LedgerWriter
{
}
```

## Scope Values

| Value | Visible from |
|-------|--------------|
| `public` | Everywhere. This is equivalent to no tag for access, but explicitly declares public API intent. |
| `root` | The outermost segment of the declaring namespace and its descendants. |
| `parent` | The declaring namespace's parent and its descendants. |
| `namespace` | The declaring namespace and its descendants. |
| `App\Billing` | The named namespace and its descendants, plus the declaring namespace. |

Several tags form a union. A declaration carrying `@visibility namespace` and `@visibility App\Console` is visible
from both subtrees. A single lowercase namespace name must have a leading backslash: `@visibility \legacy`. Without
it, the value has the shape of a misspelled keyword and is reported.

The tag may be attached to classes, interfaces, traits, enums, methods, properties, class constants, and enum cases.
A member cannot widen its containing type: both a member scope and its class-like scope must admit the reference.

## References Checked

The rule deliberately resolves written names, preserving the former standalone check's module-boundary semantics:

- instantiation, static calls, static property access, constants, enum cases, and `::class`;
- `instanceof`, `extends`, `implements`, and trait use;
- parameter, return, property, and catch types;
- attributes.

`self`, `static`, and `parent` are not reported. Member scopes are enforced for named static access and constructors.
An instance call such as `$writer->append()` is not a written class name and is not resolved by this rule. Inherited
member lookups follow parents, interfaces, and traits collected from the analysed files.

## Invalid Scopes

`customRules.visibilityInvalidScope` reports a value that cannot narrow access, including:

- an unknown lowercase keyword such as `parrent`;
- invalid namespace syntax;
- `parent` where the parent is the global namespace;
- a scope keyword on a declaration in the global namespace;
- `public` combined with any narrowing tag.

An unusable tag is reported once at its declaration. It is not silently treated as a restriction, which would create
an error at every reference without a scope anyone could satisfy.

`customRules.visibilityOutOfScope` reports the written reference. Its message names the symbol, allowed namespaces,
reference kind, and narrowest scope that would admit the caller.

## Configuration

The rule is part of `rules.neon` and follows `toolkit.allRules`. Disable only this rule with:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        visibilityScope:
            enabled: false
```

PHPStan's `paths` and `excludePaths` define both sides of the check. A declaration outside those paths is not indexed,
and a reference outside them is not collected. No separate scanner configuration is needed.

Disabling `visibilityScope` stops only the boundary rule and its collectors. The unused-symbol extensions remain
active because `@visibility public` is independent public-API metadata also consumed by other toolkit rules.

Namespaces that may cross all scopes are configured under `visibilityExemptNamespacePrefixes`. `Tests` is exempt by
default because test code commonly exercises namespace-scoped implementation details:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        visibilityExemptNamespacePrefixes:
            - Tests
            - App\Generated
```

Invalid tags are still reported on declarations inside exempt namespaces.

## Public API and Unused Findings

`@visibility public` declares that callers outside the analysed repository are expected. Such a declaration may
correctly have no local references, so the toolkit registers PHPStan always-used extensions for methods, properties,
and class constants. It also registers an ignore-error extension that suppresses declaration-unused identifiers,
including `unused` and `dead` families emitted by compatible PHPStan extensions, only when the reported declaration
line itself carries `@visibility public`.

This is semantic suppression in PHPStan's extension layer. Source-level `@phpstan-ignore` comments and baseline
entries are neither required nor generated. Unrelated errors inside the declaration remain visible.

## Fixing a Violation

Prefer moving the reference into the owning namespace or adding a public front door. Widen the tag only when the
ownership boundary is genuinely broader. Removing the tag removes the declared boundary and is not a fix.

## Rector

**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.

Changing visibility annotations or moving consumers requires an API ownership decision; automatically widening visibility would conceal the boundary violation.
